title: Verification sandbox and adjudication lattice for safe batching/caching recommendation commits
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a sandboxed verification path and an adjudication lattice that lets Optimize acceptance rules automatically decide to commit, hold, or roll back batching/caching recommendations. This ticket covers the runtime hooks, synthetic shadow traffic generator, metric adjudication ledger, and an automated rollback rehearsal flow. The approach emphasizes reproducible verification (replayable traces), multi-metric statistical gating, and minimal blast radius by exercising recommendations in a mirrored path before any production config flip.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox endpoint can accept recommendations and execute them in a mirrored runtime instance without affecting live traffic
Synthetic shadow traffic generator can replay representative request distributions and produce latency/cost/quality deltas
Adjudication ledger stores verdicts and supporting telemetry for every suggested commit (metrics, thresholds, timestamps, operator notes)
Automated decision lattice can be configured to: AUTO-COMMIT, HOLD (await operator), or AUTOMATIC-ROLLBACK based on multi-metric rules
Rollback rehearsal successfully reverts an applied recommendation in <2 minutes in 90% of trials and logs a replayable trace
Integration with Console shows per-suggestion runbook, metric deltas, and a one-click operator override
End-to-end CI test that simulates a failing quality metric triggers the rollback path and creates an incident ticket automatically
comments: 2025-11-05 - Aisha: Initial ticket created after spike. Proposal: run recommendations in a mirrored runtime (no routing change) and collect prefix-KV and per-token latency deltas. Focus first on small footprint caching tweaks and conservative batching increases.

2025-11-06 - Luca: Spiked a proof-of-concept mirror using a lightweight runtime container; observed KV hit-rate metric is stable but tail latency variance increases for 99.9th percentile. Will add synthetic heavy-tail traffic to reproduce.
2025-11-07 - Priya Shah (PM): Reviewed approach, requested explicit operator UX for hold reason and suggested including a mandatory pre-commit checklist for suggestions affecting percentiles > p95.

2025-11-08 - Design feedback (Rory Kim): Recommend the adjudication ledger include a human-readable rationale + link to the dataset used for replay. Also suggested color-blind safe severity indicators for Console.

2025-11-09 - Luca: Built synthetic traffic generator (github PR linked). Initial experiments: batching +2 tokens reduces token cost by ~13% but shows 7ms increase at p99 under burst workload. Adding a gated hold rule on p99 > 5ms prevented auto-commit in the failing cohort.

2025-11-10 - Ops (Maria Gonzales): Requested rollback rehearsal runbook. Executed a rehearsal: applied recommendation to sandbox, then triggered rollback; observed state drift in one trial due to stale KV manifests — added a reconciliation step to sync manifests before revert.

2025-11-11 - Security (Ibrahim): Asked for proof that ledger retention obeys data retention policies and that no PII is captured in the synthetic traces. We added redaction hooks and retention TTL config to the ledger service.

2025-11-12 - Aisha: Decision lattice implemented as a configurable rule graph. Next: wire Console approval button, add alerting integration (PagerDuty) for auto-rollback events, and author the operator runbook. Blocking: need approval on SLA for rollback window (ops to confirm).
implementation_notes: Technical pieces: sandbox runtime uses a namespaced runtime with read-only access to production KV manifests. Metrics exported to a separate telemetry ingestion key. Adjudication uses a small rules-engine service that evaluates Bayesian uplift for quality vs cost and produces a single verdict. Rollback rehearsal replays the inverse config change and runs smoke checks. We will add an operator override that annotates ledger entries.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic traffic may not cover rare edge-cases -> Mitigation: incorporate sampled production traces for a subset of runs under strict PII redaction
Risk: Rollback fails because of external state (e.g., file-backed caches) -> Mitigation: include pre-revert reconciliation step and a manual escrowing path
Risk: False positives on cost regressions lead to excessive holds -> Mitigation: require statistical significance over rolling window and minimum sample size before blocking auto-commit
